items.title: Apple’s Wallet Key Turns Into a Full Trip Pass, With Disney as Launch Partner
items.summary: Apple is turning Wallet from a place to store hotel keys into a live trip surface. Disney shows how far that could go when a pass starts carrying more of the trip.

items.title: U.S. Hotel Demand Is Rebounding — and It’s No Longer Just a Luxury Story
items.summary: Ten weeks of data show remarkably strong demand from business and leisure travelers. It's not just a World Cup bump.

items.title: IAG’s €1 Billion Loyalty Ambition Depends More on Banks Than Airlines
items.summary: Is Avios becoming the tail that wags the airline? IAG Loyalty wants to make a billion euros, and many of the levers it's pulling to get there have nothing to do with flying.

items.title: What Albania’s Flamingo Revolution Tells Us About Sovereign Capital’s Coastline Problem
items.summary: The largest tourism-real-estate deals increasingly arrive with a demand for exceptional treatment: special investor status, rewritten protections, consent bypassed. Albania is just the loudest case; the governance failure is the same everywhere.

items.title: Mexico’s Posadas Had Gone Too Luxury. Its Next Deals Will Even the Split.
items.summary: Posadas called its own luxury-heavy signings a ‘red flag,’ and is rebalancing as a soft quarter hit its luxury hotels hardest.

items.title: Announcing the Skift Transatlantic Summit 2026: Travel in a Fractured World
items.summary: Skift Transatlantic Summit returns for its second edition this October in Dublin, convening senior travel leaders to examine how geopolitics, shifting demand, and AI are reshaping the world's most valuable travel corridor.

items.title: Trip.com Says China’s Regulatory Crackdown Is Starting to Show Up in Its Numbers
items.summary: China's regulatory push is no longer just a compliance issue for Trip.com Group. It's now influencing how the company operates, and its near-term financial outlook.

items.title: Trip.com’s 200 Million China Goal Hinges on Near-Doubling Its Inbound Business Every Year
items.summary: Visa-free access may be bringing visitors to China, but Trip.com believes the real opportunity lies in building the infrastructure — AI, payments and local suppliers — to keep them coming.
